title: Refusal Calibration Study: Are Models Over-Refusing on Safety Benchmarks?

original_idea.title: Refusal Calibration Study: Are Models Over-Refusing on Safety Benchmarks?
original_idea.problem: Safety evaluations often count refusal rate as a safety metric, but over-refusal on benign requests is a separate failure mode that current metrics conflate with genuine safety.
original_idea.direction: Construct a paired dataset of 100 prompts: 50 genuinely harmful and 50 superficially similar but benign. Evaluate 3-4 models. Compute a 'calibration score' as the ratio of refusal rates. Identify whether models with high safety scores are simply refusing everything.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Over-refusal reduces utility without adding real safety. A calibration metric is more informative than raw refusal rate and could become a standard complementary metric.
original_idea.relevant_context: AILuminate and TrustLLM both measure refusal rates. Over-refusal has been discussed in the context of RLHF alignment but rarely operationalized as a benchmark metric.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a calibration metric directly improves how safety is measured, distinguishing genuine safety from over-refusal. Practical impact on benchmark methodology.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing paired prompts and measuring refusal rates is fully beginner-accessible. No ML training, just prompt design and basic ratio computation.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: 100 paired prompts, 3-4 models, compute ratios. Single well-defined experiment easily achievable within 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: OR-Bench (Cui et al., 2024, ICML 2025) is a large-scale over-refusal benchmark with 80,000 prompts across 10 rejection categories, plus 1,000 hard prompts and 600 toxic prompts. It directly measures the correlation between safety and over-refusal (rho=0.878). FalseReject (Zhang et al., 2025) demonstrates that safety tuning induces persistent over-refusal. SORRY-Bench (ICLR 2025) covers 45 risk categories with class-balanced sampling. The proposed 'calibration score' (ratio of refusal rates on harmful vs. benign paired prompts) is essentially what OR-Bench already operationalized at much larger scale. The idea offers no significant novel contribution beyond existing work.
